title: Robot on the line

reference.source: Reference 27: flat-ink illustration on green, 1080 × 1350 px
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: A flat green plate with a 99 px pale grid and σ 14 speckle, orange hands and a blue pole on their own plates 2 px off the 2.8 px key, and Mindgut's robot clinging to the line.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 1080 × 1350 and every length scales with the canvas

angle.does: Slope of the pole from the lower left to the upper right. Measured 53°.

shift.does: Slides the pole and both hands across the sheet.

poleW.does: Width of the striped pole, 38 px at 1.

segment.does: Pitch of the black cross bars along the pole.

shadow.does: Offset of the black band the pole throws on the ground. 0 removes it.

hand.does: Size of the two orange hands, palm 126 px at 1.

robot.does: Height of Mindgut's robot, 440 px at 1. 0 removes it.

climb.does: Where along the pole the robot clings.

ticks.does: Key strokes 70 to 140 px long beside the robot, along the pole.

grid.does: Spacing of the pale grid on the green. Measured 99 px.

gridLight.does: How pale the grid prints. The measured line is 145, 243, 192 at its center.

key.does: Width of the black line. Measured 2.8 px.

grain.does: Mottle of every ink, light specks on the green. Measured σ 14 on the green.

rough.does: How much the grain breaks each plate edge and the key.

misreg.does: Offset between plates, each in its own direction.

seed.does: Re-rolls fingers, ticks and the grain.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Open green: σ 14 speckle leaning to light specks, grid lines every 99 px

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Pole: blue plate, cross bars every 22 px, the black shadow band 38 px below

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Hand: orange plate 2 px off its key, nails in white

pass_order: key plate: the pole outline and cross bars, hand outlines with the insides cut, the robot's lines, motion ticks
object plate by id: the pole's drop shadow in key black first, then pole and robot in blue, hands in orange, nails and a dial in white
grid plate: 1.6 px lines on a 99 px pitch
one hashed grain blurred 0.6 px; the green takes it with a light-speck bias
per pixel: green with grid, then each plate at its own offset with its edge broken by the grain, the key last

measured.grid_line: center 145, 243, 192 falling to 56, 176, 117 one px out
measured.rejected: a neutral grain on the green: its speckle is skewed toward light specks, so the grain is applied with a positive-tail bias

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Green ground palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: Patches sit on the same ink in both: open green with grid lines, a pole segment with its shadow, an orange hand edge, a dense key patch, the whole sheet.

limits: Benchmark 88.8 % mean. The robot-key and pole patches score lowest (histograms 55 % and 61 %): the reference patches hold the tin robot's panel of dials and the pole's rope texture, the rebuild's hold Mindgut's plainer robot and a flat pole with cross bars, so the key share differs by position.
The green-grid patch misses on autocorrelation (86 %): the reference's grid lines are 1 to 2 px with a soft halo and the rebuild's are 2.2 px blurred 0.4 px.
The reference's tin robot is not redrawn; Mindgut's robot clings to the pole in its place, drawn with the same key.
The hands and pole are generated shapes; patches compare the same inks, not the same drawing.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
